# SMA-840: send Anthropic thinking blocks back in a tool loop

Linear: SMA-840. Builds on the SMA-827 provider-data carrier
(`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-sma-827-gemini-thought-signatures-design.md`, sections
"Core types" and the rollback note).

## Intent

With extended thinking, an Anthropic response can hold `thinking` blocks (with a signature) and
`redacted_thinking` blocks. Anthropic's documentation tells callers to send these blocks back,
unchanged, in the next request of a tool loop, so that the model keeps its reasoning. Today the
SDK drops them:

- The stream drops `signature_delta` (`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/src/stream.rs`,
  "signature_delta dropped (round-trip not yet supported)").
- The stream has no type for a `redacted_thinking` block. `model.rs` skips the unparseable
  `content_block_start` event with a warning for each block, so the block is lost.
- The request translator drops `ContentPart::Reasoning` with a warning, and it drops every
  `ContentPart::ProviderData` part.

Sven decided (2026-11-21) to build the full round trip, as the documentation describes.

## Probe results (2026-11-21)

A live probe ran against the Anthropic Messages API. Pass A used `claude-sonnet-5-5` with
`thinking: {"type":"adaptive"}` and `output_config.effort: "high"`. Pass B used
`claude-sonnet-4-5` with `thinking: {"type":"enabled","budget_tokens":2048}`. Both passes sent the
beta header `interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14`. The script and raw captures are in the session
scratchpad. They hold real signatures, so they are not in the repo.

Wire format:

- A `thinking` block starts with `content_block_start` `{"type":"thinking","thinking":"","signature":""}`.
  Then `thinking_delta` events come, then exactly one `signature_delta`, then `content_block_stop`.
- On `claude-sonnet-5-5` the thinking text is empty: only the signature arrives (988 to 1180
  characters). On `claude-sonnet-4-5` the text arrives (106 to 245 characters) with a signature
  (528 to 716 characters).
- A `redacted_thinking` block arrives whole in `content_block_start`:
  `{"type":"redacted_thinking","data":"…"}`, with no delta, then `content_block_stop`. One
  response had 15 of them (388 to 436 characters each). Only pass B produced them, with the
  documented test trigger string in the prompt.
- A `tool_use` block start now also has a `caller` key. The SDK ignores it.
- The observed block order was always thinking (or redacted blocks), then `text`, then `tool_use`.
  No response had interleaved thinking (a thinking block after a `tool_use` block in the same
  response).
- `claude-sonnet-5-5` rejects `{"type":"enabled"}` with HTTP 400: "\"thinking.type.enabled\" is not
  supported for this model. Use \"thinking.type.adaptive\" and \"output_config.effort\"". With
  adaptive thinking, it thought only on some prompts.

Second-turn requests, with thinking still on (unless the row says otherwise):

| Shape | Pass A | Pass B |
|---|---|---|
| Blocks sent back as received | 200 | 200 |
| Thinking blocks removed | 200 | 200 |
| Thinking blocks removed, thinking off | 200 | 200 |
| Thinking blocks kept, thinking off | 200 | 200 |
| One signature changed | 400 "Invalid `signature` in `thinking` block" | 400 (same) |
| `tool_use` before the thinking block | 200 | 200 |
| Thinking text changed | 200 | 200 |
| Same blocks sent to a Haiku model (`claude-haiku-5-5` / `claude-haiku-4-5`) | 200 | 200 |
| Third turn, thinking of round 1 or round 2 removed | 200 | 200 |
| 15 `redacted_thinking` blocks sent back | (none produced) | 200 |

What the probe shows:

1. Anthropic accepts a tool turn with no thinking block while thinking is on. So the SDK's tool
   loop works today, and the round trip is not needed to avoid an error. The ticket said the loop
   "does not work"; the probe does not support that.
2. Anthropic checks the signature. It does not check the block order or the thinking text. A block
   from one Claude model is accepted by another Claude model.
3. The probe cannot show that the model uses the blocks that come back. In pass B, with the
   blocks sent back, the model thought again on its second turn; with the blocks removed, it did
   not. That is one sample only.

Earlier in the conversation Sven chose "remove the `thinking` setting from a request whose current
tool turn has no signed block". Finding 1 shows that no request needs this, so the design drops
that rule.

## Goals

1. The stream keeps each `thinking` block (text and signature) and each `redacted_thinking` block
   whole, in the SMA-827 carrier, with its position in the response.
2. The request translator sends the blocks of each assistant message back unchanged, in their
   original order relative to the `text` and `tool_use` blocks of the same response.
3. Interleaved thinking (a thinking block after a `tool_use` block in the same response) keeps its
   order. The probe did not produce it, so unit tests pin it with a synthetic fixture.
4. A response with no thinking block writes no provider data. Its items, its session record and its
   next request stay byte-identical to `main`.
5. A history with no Anthropic provider data (old sessions, another provider) gives the same
   request as `main`.

## Non-goals

- Bedrock. Bedrock drops Claude reasoning signatures and redacted content in the same way
  (`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/stream.rs`). That is a separate ticket.
- A new setting for `output_config.effort`, or a change to the `ExtendedThinking` options.
- A model or API check on a block before it goes back. Finding 2 shows a cross-model block is
  accepted. A block that Anthropic rejects (for example, after a manual history edit) gives the
  API error unchanged.
- A change to how core joins reasoning text. Core keeps one `Reasoning` part per message for
  display. The request translator does not read it when blocks are present.
- Removing the `thinking` setting from any request (see the probe results).

## Anti-goals

- Provider data on responses with no thinking. The SMA-827 rollback note says that an older core
  fails on the `provider_data` variant. Every Anthropic tool turn would otherwise become
  unreadable to an older reader.
- A changed request for a history that has no Anthropic provider data.
- A failure or warning because of another provider's provider data.

## Approaches

Sven picked approach A on 2026-11-21.

- **A. One provider-data part for each block (picked).** At the stop of each block, the stream
  sends one `ProviderData { provider: "anthropic" }`. Thinking blocks carry the whole block. The
  first `text` block and each `tool_use` block carry only their index. The request translator
  sorts by index. This is the Gemini pattern, it ties each `tool_use` index to its call through
  `call_id`, and it agrees with conformance assertion 8.
- **B. One part for each response**, sent at `message_stop`, that holds the ordered block list with
  `tool_use` ids as references. Simpler to rebuild, but nothing is kept if the stream stops early,
  and the references are not tied to their calls through `call_id`.
- **Rejected: thinking first, then text, then `tool_use`.** It loses interleaved order, which the
  ticket requires.

## Design

### Carrier key and data shapes

- A new `pub const PROVIDER_DATA_KEY: &str = "anthropic";` in
  `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/src/lib.rs`, with rustdoc that states the data
  shapes below. It is a wire-format key, separate from `PROVIDER_ID` (the same string today).
- `index` is the Anthropic content-block `index` of the response (a JSON number).
- Thinking block: `call_id: None`, `data: {"index": n, "block": {"type":"thinking","thinking":"…","signature":"…"}}`.
- Redacted block: `call_id: None`, `data: {"index": n, "block": {"type":"redacted_thinking","data":"…"}}`.
- Text position: `call_id: None`, `data: {"index": n, "type": "text"}`, for the first text block of
  the response only.
- Tool-use position: `call_id: Some(id)`, `data: {"index": n}`, where `id` is the `tool_use` id.

The `block` value is the wire block exactly as Anthropic sent it, rebuilt from the stream. The
translator sends it back as it is.

### Stream (`sse.rs`, `stream.rs`)

- `ContentBlockHead` gets `RedactedThinking { data: String }` (`"redacted_thinking"`).
- `BlockState::Thinking` keeps the joined thinking text and the signature. `thinking_delta` still
  emits `ReasoningDelta` (no change for display). `signature_delta` appends to the signature.
- `BlockState::RedactedThinking { data }` holds the redacted data.
- On `content_block_stop` for index `n`:
  - Thinking with a non-empty signature: emit the thinking provider data. A thinking block with no
    signature is not sent back (Anthropic would reject it); log at debug.
  - Redacted thinking with non-empty data: emit the redacted provider data.
  - Text: record the position of the first text block.
  - `tool_use`: record the position, but only for a call that the stream emitted as a
    `ToolCallDelta` (`name_emitted`), and never for the synthesized structured-output tool
    (`synthesized_tool_index`).
- Position records wait until the response has its first thinking or redacted block. At that
  point the stream emits all waiting position records, and after it each new position is emitted at
  its block stop. When the response ends with no thinking block, the stream emits no position
  record. So a response with no thinking writes no provider data (Goal 4). The order of
  provider-data events has no meaning, because each one carries its index.
- `ContentBlockStop` for an unknown index stays a debug log.

### Core

No change. The accumulator already stores provider data in arrival order in the turn's
`AssistantMessage`, after `Reasoning` and `Text`. Tool calls stay `Item::ToolCall` items sorted by
call id. The token estimate counts the serialized length of `data` (SMA-827). Anthropic does not
bill thinking blocks of earlier turns as input, so the estimate is high for those turns; this is
accepted.

### Request translator (`translate/request.rs`)

For each assistant message, and the `tool_use` blocks that join it (`Item::ToolCall` items that
follow, and `ContentPart::ToolUse` parts in the message):

1. Collect the message's provider-data parts whose `provider` is `PROVIDER_DATA_KEY`. Ignore other
   providers' parts with no warning (SMA-827 contract).
2. If there are none: build the message exactly as `main` does today.
3. If there are some: build these blocks, each with a sort key:
   - each `block` part: its `block` value, key `index`;
   - the text: one `text` block with the message's text (blank text stays dropped), key = the text
     position index, or, with no text position, a key after every thinking block and before every
     `tool_use` block;
   - each `tool_use` block: key = the index of the position part with the same `call_id`, matched
     take-and-remove in order so that a repeated id in one message stays correct; a `tool_use` with
     no position part goes last, in today's order.
   Sort by key (stable) and send that order.
4. `ContentPart::Reasoning` is not sent. When the message has Anthropic blocks, it is dropped with
   no log. When it has none, the drop logs at debug level, not warn (the probe shows the request
   is valid without it).
5. A part with a malformed `data` (no number `index`, a `block` that is not an object with a string
   `type` of `thinking` or `redacted_thinking`) is skipped with a debug log, never an error.

Blocks go back for every assistant message in the history, not only the last one. The probe shows
that this is accepted, and the request then stays the same as the history grows. The `thinking`
setting of the request is not changed by the history.

The SMA-834 rule ("an assistant message with only `tool_use` blocks joins an open round") must
still see such a message as tool-use-only when it also carries thinking blocks. The builder checks
the shape: an assistant message of thinking plus `tool_use` that follows an open round. If the
SMA-834 test with reasoning (`request.rs` test near line 878) changes its expected output, the
builder records why.

### Conformance suite

The Anthropic conformance run must pass assertion 8 (a call-scoped `ProviderData` names a streamed
call). The `name_emitted` rule above keeps that true.

## Tests

- Fixtures, transcribed from the probe captures with fake signatures and fake redacted data, LF
  line endings (the existing `tests/fixtures/*.txt` rule):
  - `thinking_text_tool_use.txt`: thinking (text and signature), text, `tool_use` (pass B turn 1).
  - `redacted_thinking_tool_use.txt`: two `redacted_thinking` blocks, text, `tool_use`.
  - `interleaved_thinking.txt` (synthetic, marked as such in a comment): thinking, `tool_use`,
    thinking, `tool_use`.
- Stream unit tests: the provider-data events and their data for each fixture; `ReasoningDelta`
  still emitted; no provider data for the existing fixtures without thinking
  (`tool_use_then_continuation.txt`, `parallel_tool_use.txt`, a text-only fixture).
- Round-trip tests from each fixture: stream translator, then `ModelTurnAccumulator` / `build_items`,
  then `build_request`. The request's assistant content equals the original wire blocks in the
  original order, signatures included.
- Request tests: a history with no Anthropic provider data gives the same JSON as `main` (snapshot
  or explicit JSON); foreign provider data is ignored; a malformed part is skipped; a repeated
  `tool_use` id in one message; the SMA-834 shape with thinking.
- Conformance suite passes for Anthropic.
- Live tests (`tests/live.rs`, `#[ignore]`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`):
  1. A two-turn tool loop through the model with `claude-sonnet-4-5` and
     `ExtendedThinking::Enabled { budget_tokens: 2048 }`. It asserts that turn 1 gave an Anthropic
     thinking provider-data part with a non-empty signature, that the turn-2 request body holds
     that signature (the builder places this test where it can read the request body, as SMA-827
     did), and that turn 2 ends with `Finish` and no error. The model id can be changed with an
     environment variable.
  2. An `LlmAgent` loop with thinking and a real tool, ending with `Finish`.
  3. A redacted round trip with the documented trigger string. It asserts that the response had a
     redacted provider-data part and that the next turn has no error.

## Docs and release

- Crate rustdoc for `PROVIDER_DATA_KEY` and a short section in the crate docs; the Anthropic
  `README.md`; the providers page in `docs/book/src/concepts/model-providers.md`. State that the
  blocks go back unchanged, that a response with no thinking writes no provider data, and that
  `claude-sonnet-5-5` needs `ExtendedThinking::Adaptive`.
- Remove the `#[allow(dead_code)]` on the signature field.
- Additive change: the commit type is `fix(providers)`. Release-plz does the version bump. No hand
  bump.
- Rollback note for the PR: a session recorded after this change, with thinking on, holds
  `provider_data` parts; an older core cannot read it (SMA-827 note).

## Left to the builder

- Where the waiting position records live in `MessageTranslator`, and the exact helper names.
- How the request translator gets the sort keys onto the `tool_use` blocks that `push_tool_uses`
  appends (for example, by keeping the position map of the last assistant message until its
  `tool_use` blocks are in place).
- The environment variable name for the live-test model id.

content.text:
I wrote the design. It is in the worktree at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-21-sma-840-anthropic-thinking-signatures-design.md` and is not committed yet. It has these main points:

- **Probe results:** the two passes and the full table are in the document. The design does not include the rule that removes the `thinking` setting, because the probe shows that no request needs it.
- **Stream:**
  - The stream parses `redacted_thinking`.
  - When each `thinking` or `redacted_thinking` block stops, the stream sends one provider-data part with the whole block and its index.
  - The first `text` block and each `tool_use` block get a position part. A `tool_use` position part carries its `call_id`.
  - Position parts are sent only after the response has its first thinking block. So a response with no thinking writes no provider data, and its session record stays the same as on `main`.
- **Request:**
  - The translator sorts the blocks of each assistant message by index, and it sends the thinking blocks back unchanged.
  - A history with no Anthropic data gives the same request as on `main`.

Close the two BLOCKERs before implementation starts. Each needs a short probe and explicit rules, not a new approach.

  - **Thinking-only assistant messages are a new wire shape that core makes on normal paths, and no probe covers them**
    - What is wrong:
      - On `main`, an `AssistantMessage` with only `Reasoning` and provider data gives no blocks. So the hand-off turn `[thinking, tool_use transfer_to_x]` becomes `[thinking]`.
      - A `Length` finish after the thinking block, or a blank text, gives the same shape. `claude-sonnet-5-5` is not in `KNOWN_MODELS`, so it gets `max_tokens` 4096 (capabilities.rs:18-23), and adaptive thinking can use all of it.
      - No probe row covers "thinking kept, its `tool_use` and `tool_result` removed", and no row covers "assistant message with only thinking blocks".

        - `trailing_blank_user_then_reasoning_assistant_sets_flag` (request.rs:1167) no longer sets the flag. The SDK then sends a request that ends with an assistant `[thinking]` message, where `main` gives a clear SDK error.

The stream half and the data model are sound. Goal 4 keeps the stored format and the next request of every turn without thinking unchanged. The request half is not specified well enough to build, and two decisions rest on evidence that differs from what the SDK sends or what core produces. Close the two BLOCKERs before implementation starts. Each needs a short probe and explicit rules, not a new approach.

- **Thinking-only assistant messages are a new wire shape that core makes on normal paths, and no probe covers them**
  - What is wrong:
    - On `main`, an `AssistantMessage` with only `Reasoning` and provider data gives no blocks. So the hand-off turn `[thinking, tool_use transfer_to_x]` becomes `[thinking]`.
    - A `Length` finish after the thinking block, or a blank text, gives the same shape. `claude-sonnet-5-5` is not in `KNOWN_MODELS`, so it gets `max_tokens` 4096 (capabilities.rs:18-23), and adaptive thinking can use all of it.
    - No probe row covers "thinking kept, its `tool_use` and `tool_result` removed", and no row covers "assistant message with only thinking blocks".
    - Two existing behaviours also change:
      - `trailing_blank_user_then_reasoning_assistant_sets_flag` (request.rs:1167) no longer sets the flag. The SDK then sends a request that ends with an assistant `[thinking]` message, where `main` gives a clear SDK error.
      - `CacheStrategy::LastTurn` (/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-840/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/src/translate/cache.rs:53-65) then puts `cache_control` on that thinking block. Anthropic documents that a thinking block cannot carry `cache_control`.
  - Why it matters: hand-offs between Anthropic agents that have thinking on work on `main`. After this change they can fail, and there is no fallback.

The probe has four new cases, and run 3 uses the SDK default headers with no beta:

- **18:** the full history with thinking blocks, sent to a model with no thinking support. This is the `CompactingSession` case, and it uses `claude-3-5-haiku-latest`.
- **19 and 20:** a final answer with its thinking kept, and with its thinking removed, then a new user question.
- **21:** an assistant message that holds only thinking, which is the hand-off transcript case.
- **All variants** now print `input_tokens`.

Run 3 tests `claude-sonnet-4-5` and `claude-opus-4-5`, each with `enabled` thinking and a budget of 2048.

Please run it:

```
! cd /Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon && (set -a; . ./.env; set +a; bash /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-smaschek-dev-paigasus-paigasus-helikon/ebc68a6c-86b8-4a5f-80af-4e374bf8b2aa/scratchpad/probe-840-run3.sh)
```

If your account has no `claude-3-5-haiku-latest` or no `claude-opus-4-5`, give another id with `NOTHINK_MODEL=` or `OPUS_MODEL=` before `bash`.

While you run it, I will fold the findings that do not depend on the result into the design:

- **Request algorithm:** one block group for each source message. Each group sorts only inside itself, and the position map has a defined scope, as in SMA-827.
- **SMA-834 join rule:** it now also accepts `thinking` blocks.
- **Thinking-only messages:** an assistant message with no text and no `tool_use` drops its thinking blocks, as `main` drops the message today.
- **Conformance:** a new conformance scenario.
- **Live tests:** new live-test rules. The tests go in `src/`, they check the request body, and they use 4096 or more output tokens.
- **Smaller fixes:**
  - a `kind` field in the data;
  - each block is built again from known fields only;
  - a block state is removed at its stop;
  - the full list of doc changes;
  - the rollback note.

When the result is back, I will bring you one question at Gate 1. Do the blocks go back for every turn in the history, or only for the current tool loop? That choice sets the input cost.

# SMA-840: send Anthropic thinking blocks back in a tool loop

Linear: SMA-840. Builds on the SMA-827 provider-data carrier
(`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-sma-827-gemini-thought-signatures-design.md`, sections
"Core types" and the rollback note).

## Intent

With extended thinking, an Anthropic response can hold `thinking` blocks (with a signature) and
`redacted_thinking` blocks. Anthropic's documentation tells callers to send these blocks back,
unchanged, in the next request of a tool loop, so that the model keeps its reasoning. Today the
SDK drops them:

- The stream drops `signature_delta` (`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/src/stream.rs`,
  "signature_delta dropped (round-trip not yet supported)").
- The stream has no type for a `redacted_thinking` block. `model.rs` skips the unparseable
  `content_block_start` event with one warning for each block, so the block is lost.
- The request translator drops `ContentPart::Reasoning` with a warning, and it drops every
  `ContentPart::ProviderData` part.

The probe below shows the effect: Anthropic does not reject the request, but when the first
assistant message of a tool loop has no thinking block, the API turns thinking off for that request
without an error. So today the model stops thinking after its first tool call.

Sven decided (2026-11-21) to build the full round trip.

## Probe results (2026-11-21)

Three live runs against the Anthropic Messages API. The script is committed at
`docs/superpowers/probes/2026-11-21-sma-840-anthropic-thinking-probe.sh` (it reads
`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and prints no key and no signature). The raw captures hold real signatures, so
they are not in the repo.

- Run A: `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `thinking: {"type":"adaptive"}`, `output_config.effort: "high"`,
  beta `interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14`.
- Run B: `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `thinking: {"type":"enabled","budget_tokens":2048}`, same beta.
- Run C: `claude-sonnet-4-5` and `claude-opus-4-5`, `enabled` with budget 2048, **no beta header**
  (the SDK default).

Wire format:

- A `thinking` block starts with `content_block_start`
  `{"type":"thinking","thinking":"","signature":""}`. Then `thinking_delta` events, then exactly one
  `signature_delta`, then `content_block_stop`.
- On `claude-sonnet-5-5` the thinking text is empty and only the signature arrives (988 to 1180
  characters). On the 4.5 models the text arrives (106 to 256 characters) with a signature (528 to
  732 characters).
- A `redacted_thinking` block arrives whole in `content_block_start`:
  `{"type":"redacted_thinking","data":"…"}`, with no delta, then `content_block_stop`. Runs B and C
  produced 14 or 15 of them in one response (384 to 440 characters each), with the documented test
  trigger string in the prompt.
- A `tool_use` block start now also has a `caller` key. The SDK ignores it.
- The observed order was always thinking (or redacted) blocks, then `text`, then `tool_use`. No
  response had interleaved thinking inside one response.
- `claude-sonnet-5-5` rejects `{"type":"enabled"}` with HTTP 400 ("\"thinking.type.enabled\" is not
  supported for this model. Use \"thinking.type.adaptive\" and \"output_config.effort\""). With
  adaptive thinking it thought only on some prompts.
- `claude-3-5-haiku-latest` returns HTTP 404: the 3.x models are retired.

Requests (thinking on unless the row says otherwise). "Thinks" means the response has a thinking
block. Input tokens in brackets.

| Shape | Run A (5.5, beta) | Run B (4.5, beta) | Run C sonnet-4-5 / opus-4-5 (no beta) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Turn 2, blocks sent back | 200 (717) | 200, thinks (1016) | 200 (886 / 868) |
| Turn 2, thinking blocks removed | 200 (660) | 200, **does not think** (764) | 200 (785 / 778) |
| Turn 2, blocks removed, thinking off | 200 | 200 | 200 |
| Turn 2, blocks kept, thinking off | 200 | 200 | 200 |
| One signature changed | 400 "Invalid `signature` in `thinking` block" | 400 | 400 / 400 |
| `tool_use` before the thinking block | 200 | 200 | 200 |
| Thinking text changed | 200 | 200, thinks | 200 |
| Same blocks to a Haiku model | 200 | 200 | 200 |
| Turn 3, all blocks | 200 | 200, thinks (1167) | 200 (1005 / 986) |
| Turn 3, round-1 thinking removed | 200 | 200, **does not think** (871) | 200 (904 / 896) |
| Turn 3, round-2 thinking removed (the split shape) | 200 | 200, thinks (1123) | 200 (1005 / 986) |
| Redacted blocks sent back | (none produced) | 200 | 200 / 200 |
| Assistant message with only thinking, then user text | - | - | 200 / 200 |

What the probe shows:

1. Anthropic accepts every shape that this design or `main` can send, with and without the beta
   header. No request needs the `thinking` setting removed, so the design drops the rule that Sven
   chose before the probe ("remove `thinking` when the current tool turn has no signed block").
2. When the first assistant message of the tool loop has no thinking block, the API turns thinking
   off for that request with no error (run B, both "removed" rows). With the blocks sent back and the
   interleaved beta, the model thinks again after a tool result. That is the user gain.
3. Without the interleaved beta, the model does not think again inside the tool loop, with or
   without the blocks. The blocks still go into the context: they add about 100 input tokens for
   each round on run C, and about 250 to 300 on run B.
4. Anthropic checks the signature. It does not check the block order or the thinking text. A block
   from one Claude 4.x model is accepted by another.
5. Not tested: thinking blocks on an earlier user turn's final answer (the run C final answer had
   no thinking), and whether a signature is bound to an organization or an API key.

## Goals

1. The stream keeps each `thinking` block (text and signature) and each `redacted_thinking` block
   whole, in the SMA-827 carrier, with its position in the response.
2. The request translator sends the blocks of each assistant message back unchanged, in their
   original order relative to the `tool_use` blocks and the first `text` block of the same
   response.
3. Interleaved thinking (a thinking block after a `tool_use` block in the same response) keeps its
   order. The probe did not produce it, so unit tests pin it with a synthetic fixture.
4. A response with no thinking block that is sent back writes no provider data. Its items, its
   session record and its next request stay byte-identical to `main`.
5. A history with no Anthropic provider data (old sessions, another provider) gives the same
   request as `main`.

## Non-goals

- Bedrock. It drops Claude reasoning signatures and redacted content in the same way
  (`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/stream.rs`). A separate ticket.
- A setting for `output_config.effort`, an automatic interleaved-thinking beta header, or a change
  to the `ExtendedThinking` options.
- A model, API or key check on a block before it goes back. Probe finding 4 shows a cross-model
  block is accepted. A block that Anthropic rejects gives the API error unchanged; the README
  documents how a host removes the blocks (below).
- Exact text order when one response has more than one `text` block. Core joins all text of a
  turn into one `Text` part, and the stream records only the first text position. So
  `thinking, text A, tool_use, thinking, text B, tool_use` goes back as
  `thinking, text AB, tool_use, thinking, tool_use`. Probe finding 4 shows the API does not check
  order.
- A change to core. Core keeps one `Reasoning` part per message for display. The request translator
  does not read it.

## Anti-goals

- Provider data on responses with no thinking. The SMA-827 rollback note says that an older core
  fails on the `provider_data` variant.
- A changed request for a history that has no Anthropic provider data.
- A failure or warning because of another provider's provider data.
- A new failure on a shape that `main` sends today and the API accepts (hand-off transcripts,
  resumed sessions, SMA-834 joined rounds, the drop-induced prefill error).

## Approaches

Sven picked approach A on 2026-11-21.

- **A. One provider-data part for each block (picked).** At the stop of each block, the stream
  sends one `ProviderData { provider: "anthropic" }`. Thinking blocks carry the whole block. The
  first `text` block and each `tool_use` block carry only their position. The request translator
  sorts by position. This is the Gemini pattern, it ties each `tool_use` position to its call
  through `call_id`, and it agrees with conformance assertion 8.
- **B. One part for each response**, sent at `message_stop`, with the ordered block list and
  `tool_use` ids as references. Simpler to rebuild, but nothing is kept if the stream stops early,
  and the references are not tied to their calls through `call_id`.
- **Rejected: thinking first, then text, then `tool_use`.** It loses interleaved order.

## Design

### Carrier key and data shapes

- A new `pub const PROVIDER_DATA_KEY: &str = "anthropic";` in
  `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/src/lib.rs`. It is a wire-format key, separate from
  `PROVIDER_ID` (the same string today). Its rustdoc says that a host may filter parts by this key,
  but the `data` shape is private to the crate and can change.
- The crate reads and writes `data` through one private serde type with a `kind` tag:
  - `{"kind":"block","index":n,"block":{"type":"thinking","thinking":"…","signature":"…"}}`, `call_id: None`;
  - `{"kind":"block","index":n,"block":{"type":"redacted_thinking","data":"…"}}`, `call_id: None`;
  - `{"kind":"text","index":n}`, `call_id: None`, for the first text block of the response only;
  - `{"kind":"tool_use","index":n}`, `call_id: Some(id)`, where `id` is the `tool_use` id.
- `index` is the Anthropic content-block `index` of the response.

### Stream (`sse.rs`, `stream.rs`)

- `ContentBlockHead::Thinking` gets `thinking` and `signature` fields with `#[serde(default)]`;
  their values start the block state. A new `ContentBlockHead::RedactedThinking { data: String }`
  (`"redacted_thinking"`). Remove `#[allow(dead_code)]` on the signature field and on
  `ContentBlockStop::index`.
- `BlockState::Thinking` keeps the joined text and the signature. `thinking_delta` still emits
  `ReasoningDelta`. `signature_delta` appends to the signature. `BlockState::RedactedThinking`
  keeps `data`.
- On `content_block_stop` for index `n`, the stream removes the block state (a second stop for the
  same index only writes a debug log), then:
  - thinking with a non-empty signature: emit the `block` part; a thinking block with no signature
    is not kept (debug log, index and type only);
  - redacted thinking with non-empty data: emit the `block` part;
  - the first text block: record a `text` position;
  - `tool_use`: record a `tool_use` position, but only for a call that the stream emitted as a
    `ToolCallDelta` (`name_emitted`), and never for the synthesized structured-output tool
    (`synthesized_tool_index`).
- Position records wait until the stream emits the response's first `block` part. Then the stream
  emits all waiting records, and after that each new position at its block stop. If the response
  emits no `block` part, it emits no position record (Goal 4). Provider-data order has no meaning,
  because each part carries its index.
- Log lines hold only the index and the block type, never block content.

### Core

No change. The accumulator stores provider data in arrival order in the turn's `AssistantMessage`,
after `Reasoning` and `Text`. Tool calls stay `Item::ToolCall` items sorted by call id. The token
estimate counts the `Reasoning` text and the serialized `data` (which holds the text again and the
signature). So the estimate is high on models that strip earlier thinking and close on models that
keep it in context; this is accepted and documented.

### Request translator (`translate/request.rs`)

Terms: a **source message** is one `Item::AssistantMessage` together with the `tool_use` blocks
that come from it: its own `ContentPart::ToolUse` parts, and the `Item::ToolCall` items that follow
it before the next `AssistantMessage` or the next user message with a part that is not a tool
result. A `ToolResult` does not end a source message (the SMA-827 Gemini rule).

1. **Position map.** For each source message, collect its parts with
   `provider == PROVIDER_DATA_KEY` that parse as the private type. Ignore other providers' parts with
   no log. Skip a part that does not parse, or a `block` that fails the checks below, with a debug
   log. A source message with no valid Anthropic part builds exactly as on `main`.
2. **Block checks.** Rebuild each block from known fields only: `thinking` needs string `thinking`
   (an empty string is valid) and a non-empty string `signature`; `redacted_thinking` needs a
   non-empty string `data`. Send only `type` and those fields.
3. **Groups.** Each wire assistant message is a list of groups, one group for each source message
   that adds blocks to it, in the order the groups are added. Inside a group, each block gets a sort
   key:
   - a `block` part: its `index`;
   - the text block: the `text` position index; with no `text` position, the key is just before
     the first `tool_use` block of the group in key order, or after every block when the group has
     no `tool_use`;
   - a `tool_use` block: the index of the `tool_use` position part with the same `call_id`, taken
     and removed in order, so that a repeated id in one source message stays correct; with no
     position, it goes after every keyed block, in today's order.
   A position part whose `tool_use` is gone (trimmed history) is ignored.
4. **Sort.** Sort each group by key (stable), and never compare keys of different groups. Do the
   sort in one pass at the end of `translate_messages`, before `apply_cache_strategy`. A `tool_use`
   that `close_open_transfers` or another split moves into a different wire message loses its key
   and goes after the keyed blocks of its new message.
5. **Thinking-only messages.** A wire assistant message that, after all its `tool_use` blocks
   join, has no `text` and no `tool_use` block drops its thinking blocks. It then counts as empty,
   exactly as on `main` (no flush, not sent, the drop-induced prefill flag unchanged). The decision
   looks ahead over the items, because the `tool_use` blocks come from later items. This keeps
   hand-off transcripts (`thread_handoff_transcript` removes tool calls and keeps assistant
   messages), `Length` finishes after a thinking block, and
   `trailing_blank_user_then_reasoning_assistant_sets_flag` as on `main`.
6. **SMA-834 join rule.** An assistant message joins an open round when every block is
   `tool_use`, `thinking` or `redacted_thinking`, the pending results are not empty, and the round
   is open. This covers the nested form (`[ProviderData thinking, ToolUse]`) and the form that the
   accumulator writes (`AssistantMessage[Reasoning, ProviderData]` then `Item::ToolCall`).
7. **Reasoning.** `ContentPart::Reasoning` is never sent. Its drop logs at debug level, not warn.
8. **Cache.** `apply_cache_strategy` never puts `cache_control` on a `thinking` or
   `redacted_thinking` block. If the last block is one of them, it uses the last other block of
   that message, or no breakpoint.
9. **Which turns.** See "Open question for Sven". The `thinking` setting of the request is not
   changed by the history.

### Conformance suite

Add an Anthropic scenario with a thinking block and a `tool_use` block, transcribed from the
`thinking_text_tool_use.txt` fixture under the suite's provenance rule. Other subjects decline it.
Assertion 8 then checks the Anthropic `tool_use` positions.

## Open question for Sven

Which assistant messages send their blocks back?

- **All messages in the history (my pick).** This follows Anthropic's advice to send the history
  unchanged. The API decides what to keep, so models that keep earlier thinking in context get it.
  The request prefix stays the same as the history grows, which keeps the prompt cache valid.
- **Only the current tool loop** (assistant messages after the last real user message). The input
  cost is lower on models that keep earlier thinking, and a bad block leaves the history at the next
  user message. But the request prefix changes at each new user message.

## Recovery and privacy (README)

- One rejected block makes each later request of that session fail. A host recovers by removing
  every part with `provider == PROVIDER_DATA_KEY` from the stored history; the next request is then
  the `main` request.
- The thinking text is stored two times: in the `Reasoning` part and in the `block` data. A host
  that removes `Reasoning` before storage must also remove these parts.

## Tests

- Fixtures, transcribed from the probe captures with fake signatures and fake redacted data, LF line
  endings (the existing `tests/fixtures/*.txt` rule):
  - `thinking_text_tool_use.txt`: thinking (text and signature), text, `tool_use` (run C turn 1);
  - `redacted_thinking_tool_use.txt`: two `redacted_thinking` blocks, text, `tool_use`;
  - `empty_thinking_tool_use.txt`: thinking with empty text and a signature, text, `tool_use`
    (run A);
  - `interleaved_thinking.txt` (synthetic, marked as such in a comment): thinking, `tool_use`,
    thinking, `tool_use`;
  - `unsigned_thinking_tool_use.txt` (synthetic): a thinking block with no `signature_delta`, then
    `tool_use`.
- Stream unit tests: the provider-data events for each fixture; `ReasoningDelta` still emitted; no
  provider data for the unsigned fixture and for the fixtures without thinking
  (`tool_use_then_continuation.txt`, `parallel_tool_use.txt`); the existing `thinking_then_text.txt`
  now emits a `block` part and a `text` position; a `tool_use` with no `input_json_delta` gives no
  position; a repeated `content_block_stop` emits nothing new.
- Round-trip tests from each fixture: stream translator, then `ModelTurnAccumulator::finish`, then
  `translate_messages` / `build_body`. The assistant content equals the original wire blocks in the
  original order, with the text rule above.
- A session round trip, as in SMA-827: `SessionRecorder`, then `project()`, then the translator.
- Request tests: a history with no Anthropic provider data gives the same JSON as `main`; foreign
  provider data is ignored; a malformed part and a failed block check are skipped; a repeated
  `tool_use` id; an orphan position part; the SMA-834 parity test with thinking in both forms; a
  hand-off transcript (thinking-only message); `reasoning_only_assistant_is_not_sent` and
  `trailing_blank_user_then_reasoning_assistant_sets_flag` with Anthropic blocks added; the
  `close_open_transfers` split; `cache_control` with `CacheStrategy::LastTurn` never on a thinking
  block.
- The structured-output guard (`synthesized_tool_index`) is tested with a synthetic fixture only.
  Anthropic rejects a forced `tool_choice` with thinking on, so this path is not live.
- Conformance suite: the new Anthropic scenario passes.
- Live tests, in `src/` under `#[cfg(test)] #[ignore]` so that they can call `build_body`, with
  `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, the SDK default headers, `claude-sonnet-4-5` (the model id can be changed
  with an environment variable), `ExtendedThinking::Enabled { budget_tokens: 2048 }` and
  `max_output_tokens` of 4096 or more:
  1. A two-turn loop through the model. The prompt asks for the tool call; if turn 1 has no tool
     call or no thinking `block` part, the test fails with a clear message. It asserts that the
     turn-2 body holds the turn-1 signature, and that turn 2 ends with `Finish` and no error.
  2. An `LlmAgent` loop with a real tool and a recording `Model` wrapper that keeps each
     `ModelRequest`. It asserts that the second request, through `build_body`, holds the signature,
     and that the run completes.
  3. A redacted round trip with the documented trigger string. It asserts that the turn-2 body
     holds every redacted `data` value, and that turn 2 has no error.
  4. Test 1 again with `.beta("interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14")`. It asserts that turn 2 has a
     thinking block again. (Run B saw this once; if it fails by chance, the test message says so.)

## Docs and release

- Crate rustdoc for `PROVIDER_DATA_KEY` and a short crate-docs section; the Anthropic `README.md`
  (the round trip, the interleaved beta for 4.x `Enabled` models, `claude-sonnet-5-5` needs
  `ExtendedThinking::Adaptive`, the cost, recovery and privacy notes); `settings.rs` docs (the
  `claude-sonnet-5-5` line).
- The book: `docs/book/src/concepts/model-providers.md`; `core-primitives.md` (it names only the
  Gemini key); `sessions.md` near line 276 (it gives Gemini as the only reason for provider data);
  `agent-loop.md` (on `claude-sonnet-5-5`, a tool-only turn now gives a `MessageOutput` that holds
  only provider data, because its thinking text is empty).
- Additive change: the commit type is `fix(providers)`. Release-plz does the version bump.
- PR rollback note: core does not change, so a rollback of only the Anthropic crate is safe (the old
  translator drops the parts and sends the `main` request). A rollback of core below the SMA-827
  version stays unsafe, and more sessions are affected than with Gemini, because every Anthropic
  turn with a kept thinking block writes the variant, text-only turns too.
- The commit body states the cost: sending the blocks back adds input tokens.

## Left to the builder

- Where the waiting position records live in `MessageTranslator`, and helper names.
- The data structure for the groups in `translate_messages`.
- The environment variable name for the live-test model id.

   order. The probe did not produce it, so unit tests pin it with a synthetic fixture.
4. A response with no thinking block that is sent back writes no provider data. Its items, its
   session record and its next request stay byte-identical to `main`.
5. A history with no Anthropic provider data (old sessions, another provider) gives the same
   request as `main`.

## Non-goals

- Bedrock. It drops Claude reasoning signatures and redacted content in the same way
  (`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/stream.rs`). A separate ticket.
- A setting for `output_config.effort`, an automatic interleaved-thinking beta header, or a change
  to the `ExtendedThinking` options.
- A model, API or key check on a block before it goes back. Probe finding 4 shows a cross-model
  block is accepted. A block that Anthropic rejects gives the API error unchanged; the README
  documents how a host removes the blocks (below).
- Exact text order when one response has more than one `text` block. Core joins all text of a
  turn into one `Text` part, and the stream records only the first text position. So
  `thinking, text A, tool_use, thinking, text B, tool_use` goes back as
  `thinking, text AB, tool_use, thinking, tool_use`. Probe finding 4 shows the API does not check
  order.
- A change to core. Core keeps one `Reasoning` part per message for display. The request translator
  does not read it.

## Anti-goals

- Provider data on responses with no thinking. The SMA-827 rollback note says that an older core
  fails on the `provider_data` variant.
- A changed request for a history that has no Anthropic provider data.
- A failure or warning because of another provider's provider data.
- A new failure on a shape that `main` sends today and the API accepts (hand-off transcripts,
  resumed sessions, SMA-834 joined rounds, the drop-induced prefill error).

## Approaches

Sven picked approach A on 2026-11-21.

- **A. One provider-data part for each block (picked).** At the stop of each block, the stream
  sends one `ProviderData { provider: "anthropic" }`. Thinking blocks carry the whole block. The
  first `text` block and each `tool_use` block carry only their position. The request translator
  sorts by position. This is the Gemini pattern, it ties each `tool_use` position to its call
  through `call_id`, and it agrees with conformance assertion 8.
- **B. One part for each response**, sent at `message_stop`, with the ordered block list and
  `tool_use` ids as references. Simpler to rebuild, but nothing is kept if the stream stops early,
  and the references are not tied to their calls through `call_id`.
- **Rejected: thinking first, then text, then `tool_use`.** It loses interleaved order.

## Design

### Carrier key and data shapes

- A new `pub const PROVIDER_DATA_KEY: &str = "anthropic";` in
  `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/src/lib.rs`. It is a wire-format key, separate from
  `PROVIDER_ID` (the same string today). Its rustdoc says that a host may filter parts by this key,
  but the `data` shape is private to the crate and can change.
- The crate reads and writes `data` through one private serde type with a `kind` tag:
  - `{"kind":"block","index":n,"block":{"type":"thinking","thinking":"…","signature":"…"}}`, `call_id: None`;
  - `{"kind":"block","index":n,"block":{"type":"redacted_thinking","data":"…"}}`, `call_id: None`;
  - `{"kind":"text","index":n}`, `call_id: None`, for the first text block of the response only;
  - `{"kind":"tool_use","index":n}`, `call_id: Some(id)`, where `id` is the `tool_use` id.
- `index` is the Anthropic content-block `index` of the response.

### Stream (`sse.rs`, `stream.rs`)

- `ContentBlockHead::Thinking` gets `thinking` and `signature` fields with `#[serde(default)]`;
  their values start the block state. A new `ContentBlockHead::RedactedThinking { data: String }`
  (`"redacted_thinking"`). Remove `#[allow(dead_code)]` on the signature field and on
  `ContentBlockStop::index`.
- `BlockState::Thinking` keeps the joined text and the signature. `thinking_delta` still emits
  `ReasoningDelta`. `signature_delta` appends to the signature. `BlockState::RedactedThinking`
  keeps `data`.
- On `content_block_stop` for index `n`, the stream removes the block state (a second stop for the
  same index only writes a debug log), then:
  - thinking with a non-empty signature: emit the `block` part; a thinking block with no signature
    is not kept (debug log, index and type only);
  - redacted thinking with non-empty data: emit the `block` part;
  - the first text block: record a `text` position;
  - `tool_use`: record a `tool_use` position, but only for a call that the stream emitted as a
    `ToolCallDelta` (`name_emitted`), and never for the synthesized structured-output tool
    (`synthesized_tool_index`).

  emits all waiting records, and after that each new position at its block stop. If the response
  emits no `block` part, it emits no position record (Goal 4). Provider-data order has no meaning,
  because each part carries its index.
- Log lines hold only the index and the block type, never block content.

No change. The accumulator stores provider data in arrival order in the turn's `AssistantMessage`,
after `Reasoning` and `Text`. Tool calls stay `Item::ToolCall` items sorted by call id. The token
estimate counts the `Reasoning` text and the serialized `data` (which holds the text again and the
signature). So the estimate is high on models that strip earlier thinking and close on models that
keep it in context; this is accepted and documented.

### Request translator (`translate/request.rs`)

Terms: a **source message** is one `Item::AssistantMessage` together with the `tool_use` blocks
that come from it: its own `ContentPart::ToolUse` parts, and the `Item::ToolCall` items that follow
it before the next `AssistantMessage` or the next user message with a part that is not a tool
result. A `ToolResult` does not end a source message (the SMA-827 Gemini rule).

1. **Position map.** For each source message, collect its parts with
   `provider == PROVIDER_DATA_KEY` that parse as the private type. Ignore other providers' parts with
   no log. Skip a part that does not parse, or a `block` that fails the checks below, with a debug
   log. A source message with no valid Anthropic part builds exactly as on `main`.
2. **Block checks.** Rebuild each block from known fields only: `thinking` needs string `thinking`
   (an empty string is valid) and a non-empty string `signature`; `redacted_thinking` needs a
   non-empty string `data`. Send only `type` and those fields.
3. **Groups.** Each wire assistant message is a list of groups, one group for each source message
   that adds blocks to it, in the order the groups are added. Inside a group, each block gets a sort
   key:
   - a `block` part: its `index`;
   - the text block: the `text` position index; with no `text` position, the key is just before
     the first `tool_use` block of the group in key order, or after every block when the group has
     no `tool_use`;
   - a `tool_use` block: the index of the `tool_use` position part with the same `call_id`, taken
     and removed in order, so that a repeated id in one source message stays correct; with no
     position, it goes after every keyed block, in today's order.
   A position part whose `tool_use` is gone (trimmed history) is ignored.
4. **Sort.** Sort each group by key (stable), and never compare keys of different groups. Do the
   sort in one pass at the end of `translate_messages`, before `apply_cache_strategy`. A `tool_use`
   that `close_open_transfers` or another split moves into a different wire message loses its key
   and goes after the keyed blocks of its new message.
5. **Thinking-only messages.** A wire assistant message that, after all its `tool_use` blocks
   join, has no `text` and no `tool_use` block drops its thinking blocks. It then counts as empty,
   exactly as on `main` (no flush, not sent, the drop-induced prefill flag unchanged). The decision
   looks ahead over the items, because the `tool_use` blocks come from later items. This keeps
   hand-off transcripts (`thread_handoff_transcript` removes tool calls and keeps assistant
   messages), `Length` finishes after a thinking block, and
   `trailing_blank_user_then_reasoning_assistant_sets_flag` as on `main`.
6. **SMA-834 join rule.** An assistant message joins an open round when every block is
   `tool_use`, `thinking` or `redacted_thinking`, the pending results are not empty, and the round
   is open. This covers the nested form (`[ProviderData thinking, ToolUse]`) and the form that the
   accumulator writes (`AssistantMessage[Reasoning, ProviderData]` then `Item::ToolCall`).
7. **Reasoning.** `ContentPart::Reasoning` is never sent. Its drop logs at debug level, not warn.
8. **Cache.** `apply_cache_strategy` never puts `cache_control` on a `thinking` or
   `redacted_thinking` block. If the last block is one of them, it uses the last other block of
   that message, or no breakpoint.
9. **Which turns.** See "Open question for Sven". The `thinking` setting of the request is not
   changed by the history.

### Conformance suite

Add an Anthropic scenario with a thinking block and a `tool_use` block, transcribed from the
`thinking_text_tool_use.txt` fixture under the suite's provenance rule. Other subjects decline it.
Assertion 8 then checks the Anthropic `tool_use` positions.

## Open question for Sven

- **All messages in the history (my pick).** This follows Anthropic's advice to send the history
  unchanged. The API decides what to keep, so models that keep earlier thinking in context get it.
  The request prefix stays the same as the history grows, which keeps the prompt cache valid.
- **Only the current tool loop** (assistant messages after the last real user message). The input
  cost is lower on models that keep earlier thinking, and a bad block leaves the history at the next
  user message. But the request prefix changes at each new user message.

## Recovery and privacy (README)

- One rejected block makes each later request of that session fail. A host recovers by removing
  every part with `provider == PROVIDER_DATA_KEY` from the stored history; the next request is then
  the `main` request.
- The thinking text is stored two times: in the `Reasoning` part and in the `block` data. A host
  that removes `Reasoning` before storage must also remove these parts.

  `max_output_tokens` of 4096 or more:
  1. A two-turn loop through the model. The prompt asks for the tool call; if turn 1 has no tool
     call or no thinking `block` part, the test fails with a clear message. It asserts that the
     turn-2 body holds the turn-1 signature, and that turn 2 ends with `Finish` and no error.
  2. An `LlmAgent` loop with a real tool and a recording `Model` wrapper that keeps each

- Where the waiting position records live in `MessageTranslator`, and helper names.
- The data structure for the groups in `translate_messages`.
- The environment variable name for the live-test model id.

# SMA-840: send Anthropic thinking blocks back in a tool loop

Linear: SMA-840. Builds on the SMA-827 provider-data carrier
(`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-sma-827-gemini-thought-signatures-design.md`, sections
"Core types" and the rollback note).

## Intent

With extended thinking, an Anthropic response can hold `thinking` blocks (with a signature) and
`redacted_thinking` blocks. Anthropic's documentation tells callers to send these blocks back,
unchanged, in the next request of a tool loop, so that the model keeps its reasoning. Today the
SDK drops them:

- The stream drops `signature_delta` (`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/src/stream.rs`,
  "signature_delta dropped (round-trip not yet supported)").
- The stream has no type for a `redacted_thinking` block. `model.rs` skips the unparseable
  `content_block_start` event with one warning for each block, so the block is lost.
- The request translator drops `ContentPart::Reasoning` with a warning, and it drops every
  `ContentPart::ProviderData` part.

The probe below shows the effect: Anthropic does not reject the request, but when the first
assistant message of a tool loop has no thinking block, the API turns thinking off for that request
without an error. So today the model stops thinking after its first tool call.

Sven decided (2026-11-21) to build the full round trip.

## Probe results (2026-11-21)

Three live runs against the Anthropic Messages API. The script is committed at
`docs/superpowers/probes/2026-11-21-sma-840-anthropic-thinking-probe.sh` (it reads
`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and prints no key and no signature). The raw captures hold real signatures, so
they are not in the repo.

- Run A: `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `thinking: {"type":"adaptive"}`, `output_config.effort: "high"`,
  beta `interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14`.
- Run B: `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `thinking: {"type":"enabled","budget_tokens":2048}`, same beta.
- Run C: `claude-sonnet-4-5` and `claude-opus-4-5`, `enabled` with budget 2048, **no beta header**
  (the SDK default).

Wire format:

- A `thinking` block starts with `content_block_start`
  `{"type":"thinking","thinking":"","signature":""}`. Then `thinking_delta` events, then exactly one
  `signature_delta`, then `content_block_stop`.
- On `claude-sonnet-5-5` the thinking text is empty and only the signature arrives (988 to 1180
  characters). On the 4.5 models the text arrives (106 to 256 characters) with a signature (528 to
  732 characters).
- A `redacted_thinking` block arrives whole in `content_block_start`:
  `{"type":"redacted_thinking","data":"…"}`, with no delta, then `content_block_stop`. Runs B and C
  produced 14 or 15 of them in one response (384 to 440 characters each), with the documented test
  trigger string in the prompt.
- A `tool_use` block start now also has a `caller` key. The SDK ignores it.
- The observed order was always thinking (or redacted) blocks, then `text`, then `tool_use`. No
  response had interleaved thinking inside one response.
- `claude-sonnet-5-5` rejects `{"type":"enabled"}` with HTTP 400 ("\"thinking.type.enabled\" is not
  supported for this model. Use \"thinking.type.adaptive\" and \"output_config.effort\""). With
  adaptive thinking it thought only on some prompts.
- `claude-3-5-haiku-latest` returns HTTP 404: the 3.x models are retired.

Requests (thinking on unless the row says otherwise). "Thinks" means the response has a thinking
block. Input tokens in brackets.

| Shape | Run A (5.5, beta) | Run B (4.5, beta) | Run C sonnet-4-5 / opus-4-5 (no beta) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Turn 2, blocks sent back | 200 (717) | 200, thinks (1016) | 200 (886 / 868) |
| Turn 2, thinking blocks removed | 200 (660) | 200, **does not think** (764) | 200 (785 / 778) |
| Turn 2, blocks removed, thinking off | 200 | 200 | 200 |
| Turn 2, blocks kept, thinking off | 200 | 200 | 200 |
| One signature changed | 400 "Invalid `signature` in `thinking` block" | 400 | 400 / 400 |
| `tool_use` before the thinking block | 200 | 200 | 200 |
| Thinking text changed | 200 | 200, thinks | 200 |
| Same blocks to a Haiku model | 200 | 200 | 200 |
| Turn 3, all blocks | 200 | 200, thinks (1167) | 200 (1005 / 986) |
| Turn 3, round-1 thinking removed | 200 | 200, **does not think** (871) | 200 (904 / 896) |
| Turn 3, round-2 thinking removed (the split shape) | 200 | 200, thinks (1123) | 200 (1005 / 986) |
| Redacted blocks sent back | (none produced) | 200 | 200 / 200 |
| Assistant message with only thinking, then user text | - | - | 200 / 200 |

What the probe shows:

1. Anthropic accepts every shape that this design or `main` can send, with and without the beta
   header. No request needs the `thinking` setting removed, so the design drops the rule that Sven
   chose before the probe ("remove `thinking` when the current tool turn has no signed block").
2. When the first assistant message of the tool loop has no thinking block, the API turns thinking
   off for that request with no error (run B, both "removed" rows). With the blocks sent back and the
   interleaved beta, the model thinks again after a tool result. That is the user gain.
3. Without the interleaved beta, the model does not think again inside the tool loop, with or
   without the blocks. The blocks still go into the context: they add about 100 input tokens for
   each round on run C, and about 250 to 300 on run B.
4. Anthropic checks the signature. It does not check the block order or the thinking text. A block
   from one Claude 4.x model is accepted by another.
5. Not tested: thinking blocks on an earlier user turn's final answer (the run C final answer had
   no thinking), and whether a signature is bound to an organization or an API key.

result. A `ToolResult` does not end a source message (the SMA-827 Gemini rule).

1. **Position map.** For each source message, collect its parts with
   `provider == PROVIDER_DATA_KEY` that parse as the private type. Ignore other providers' parts with
   no log. Skip a part that does not parse, or a `block` that fails the checks below, with a debug
   log. A source message with no valid Anthropic part builds exactly as on `main`.
2. **Block checks.** Rebuild each block from known fields only: `thinking` needs string `thinking`
   (an empty string is valid) and a non-empty string `signature`; `redacted_thinking` needs a
   non-empty string `data`. Send only `type` and those fields.
3. **Groups.** Each wire assistant message is a list of groups, one group for each source message
   that adds blocks to it, in the order the groups are added. Inside a group, each block gets a sort
   key:
   - a `block` part: its `index`;
   - the text block: the `text` position index; with no `text` position, the key is just before
     the first `tool_use` block of the group in key order, or after every block when the group has
     no `tool_use`;
   - a `tool_use` block: the index of the `tool_use` position part with the same `call_id`, taken
     and removed in order, so that a repeated id in one source message stays correct; with no
     position, it goes after every keyed block, in today's order.
   A position part whose `tool_use` is gone (trimmed history) is ignored.
4. **Sort.** Sort each group by key (stable), and never compare keys of different groups. Do the
   sort in one pass at the end of `translate_messages`, before `apply_cache_strategy`. A `tool_use`
   that `close_open_transfers` or another split moves into a different wire message loses its key
   and goes after the keyed blocks of its new message.
5. **Thinking-only messages.** A wire assistant message that, after all its `tool_use` blocks
   join, has no `text` and no `tool_use` block drops its thinking blocks. It then counts as empty,
   exactly as on `main` (no flush, not sent, the drop-induced prefill flag unchanged). The decision
   looks ahead over the items, because the `tool_use` blocks come from later items. This keeps
   hand-off transcripts (`thread_handoff_transcript` removes tool calls and keeps assistant
   messages), `Length` finishes after a thinking block, and
   `trailing_blank_user_then_reasoning_assistant_sets_flag` as on `main`.
6. **SMA-834 join rule.** An assistant message joins an open round when every block is
   `tool_use`, `thinking` or `redacted_thinking`, the pending results are not empty, and the round
   is open. This covers the nested form (`[ProviderData thinking, ToolUse]`) and the form that the
   accumulator writes (`AssistantMessage[Reasoning, ProviderData]` then `Item::ToolCall`).
7. **Reasoning.** `ContentPart::Reasoning` is never sent. Its drop logs at debug level, not warn.
8. **Cache.** `apply_cache_strategy` never puts `cache_control` on a `thinking` or
   `redacted_thinking` block. If the last block is one of them, it uses the last other block of
   that message, or no breakpoint.
9. **Which turns.** See "Open question for Sven". The `thinking` setting of the request is not
   changed by the history.

## Open question for Sven

Which assistant messages send their blocks back?

- **All messages in the history (my pick).** This follows Anthropic's advice to send the history
  unchanged. The API decides what to keep, so models that keep earlier thinking in context get it.
  The request prefix stays the same as the history grows, which keeps the prompt cache valid.
- **Only the current tool loop** (assistant messages after the last real user message). The input
  cost is lower on models that keep earlier thinking, and a bad block leaves the history at the next
  user message. But the request prefix changes at each new user message.

## Recovery and privacy (README)

- One rejected block makes each later request of that session fail. A host recovers by removing
  every part with `provider == PROVIDER_DATA_KEY` from the stored history; the next request is then
  the `main` request.
- The thinking text is stored two times: in the `Reasoning` part and in the `block` data. A host
  that removes `Reasoning` before storage must also remove these parts.

I have finished **Gate 1: spec approval**. The design needs your approval and one decision from you.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-21-sma-840-anthropic-thinking-signatures-design.md` in the worktree. The probe script is at `docs/superpowers/probes/2026-11-21-sma-840-anthropic-thinking-probe.sh`. It has no key and no signatures. Neither file is committed yet.

**Challenger verdict:** APPROVE WITH CHANGES (2 BLOCKER, 6 MAJOR, 13 MINOR, 4 questions). I ran the probe a third time for BLOCKER 2.

**Probe result that changes the reason for the ticket:** the tool loop does not fail today. When the first assistant message of the loop has no thinking block, the API turns thinking off for that request with no error. So today the model stops thinking after its first tool call. With the blocks sent back and the interleaved beta header, the model thinks again (run B). Without the beta header, it does not think again in the loop. The blocks still go into the context, for about 100 more input tokens for each round.

**Folded into the spec:**

- **BLOCKER 1 (thinking-only messages):** an assistant message with no text and no `tool_use` drops its thinking blocks. Hand-off transcripts, `Length` finishes and the prefill-error test then stay as on `main`.
- **BLOCKER 2 (the probe sent a beta header that the SDK does not send):** run C used the SDK default headers on `claude-sonnet-4-5` and `claude-opus-4-5`. Every shape gave 200, including the split shape and a thinking-only message. Your earlier rule to remove `thinking` stays out, because no request needs it.
- **MAJOR:**
  - The request algorithm is now fully specified. Each source message is one group, and blocks sort only inside their group. The position map has the SMA-827 scope, and the sort runs before the cache step.
  - The SMA-834 join rule now accepts thinking blocks, in both message forms.
  - The cost is stated with the measured tokens. The estimate behavior and the doc changes are listed.
  - There is a new Anthropic conformance scenario, so assertion 8 runs.
  - A host can recover by removing the Anthropic parts. This is in the README section.
  - The live tests moved to `src/`, with checks of the request body, 4096 or more output tokens, the default headers, and an interleaved-beta variant.
- **MINOR:**
  - The data has a `kind` tag.
  - Each block is built again from known fields only. An empty thinking text is valid.
  - A block state is removed at its stop.
  - The values in the thinking block start are kept.
  - The flush starts at the first emitted block.
  - The cache never marks a thinking block.
  - The text-order loss is now a stated non-goal.
  - The doc list, the rollback note and the test names are complete.
- **Builder check:** I answered all 8 questions in the spec.

**Rejected:**

- **A builder flag to turn the round trip off:** the README recovery procedure covers the same need.
- **Splitting joined text by character counts:** the API does not check order, so this is a non-goal.
- **A version field in `data`:** the `data` shape is private to the crate.
- **A probe through `build_body`:** run C sent the same headers and body shape, and the live tests use `build_body`.

**Open after the probe:**

- whether a signature is bound to an organization or an API key;
- thinking on an earlier final answer, because run C's final answer had no thinking.

**Your decision: which assistant messages send their blocks back?**

- **All messages in the history (my pick).** Anthropic advises sending the history unchanged, and the API decides what to keep. The request prefix stays stable, so the prompt cache stays valid.
- **Only the current tool loop.** This costs less on models that keep earlier thinking, and a bad block leaves the history at the next user message. But the request prefix changes at each new user message.

Please choose one, and approve the spec or ask for changes. I also propose to file a separate Linear ticket for the same gap in Bedrock. Do you want that?

input.title: Bedrock provider drops Claude reasoning signatures and redacted content, so thinking stops after the first tool call
input.description:
The Bedrock provider drops the signature and the redacted content of Claude reasoning. The stream emits `ReasoningContentBlockDelta::Text` as a `ReasoningDelta`, but it drops `Signature` and `RedactedContent` (`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/stream.rs`, "round-trip not yet supported").

The Anthropic probe for SMA-840 shows what this does on the Anthropic API. When the first assistant message of a tool loop has no thinking block, the API does not fail. It turns thinking off for that request. So the model stops thinking after its first tool call. Bedrock Converse has the same rule for Claude models, but nobody has probed Bedrock yet.

## Required behavior

* Keep each Claude reasoning block (text and signature) and each redacted block whole in the SMA-827 provider-data carrier, with a Bedrock wire-format key.
* Send the blocks back unchanged in the next Converse request, in their original order before the `toolUse` blocks of the same turn.
* A history with no Bedrock provider data gives the same request as today.

## Acceptance criteria

* A live probe against Bedrock Converse confirms the wire format and the accepted shapes before implementation.
* A live test runs a two-turn tool loop with Claude reasoning on and checks that the second request holds the signature.
* Unit tests pin the round trip: stream to item, then item to request.

+++ Agent notes

* Follow the SMA-840 design for Anthropic: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-21-sma-840-anthropic-thinking-signatures-design.md` (SMA-840 branch). In particular, see the data shapes, the group sort, the rule for thinking-only messages, the SMA-834 join rule and the cache rule.
* The probe script `docs/superpowers/probes/2026-11-21-sma-840-anthropic-thinking-probe.sh` targets the Anthropic API. For Bedrock, it needs a Converse version.

+++

input.description: Write SMA-840 implementation plan
input.prompt:
You write an implementation plan for a Rust SDK change. First read the skill file /Users/smaschek/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/superpowers/7.0.2/skills/writing-plans/SKILL.md and follow it exactly (header, Global Constraints, Review Focus, task structure, self-review). Do not ask the user questions; the execution method is already chosen (subagent-driven), so end with the "already supplied" handoff line in your report only.

Work in the git worktree /Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-840 (branch feature/sma-840-anthropic-provider-drops-thinking-signatures). Run every shell command with `cd <worktree> || exit 1`. Use worktree-absolute paths for every file write. Do NOT run any git command that moves HEAD or a branch (no checkout/switch/reset/rebase/stash/merge/pull). Do not read .env. Do not dispatch subagents. Work in the foreground.

Inputs:
- The approved, binding spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-21-sma-840-anthropic-thinking-signatures-design.md. Read it fully. The spec wins over anything else.
- Format reference (a plan for the sister ticket): if it exists on main, docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-20-sma-827-gemini-thought-signatures.md. Use it for style, not for content.
- The code: crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/src/{sse.rs,stream.rs,model.rs,lib.rs,settings.rs,builder.rs,translate/request.rs,translate/mod.rs,translate/cache.rs}, crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/tests/ (fixtures, messages_streaming.rs, live.rs), crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/{model.rs,item.rs,loop_state.rs,session*.rs}, tests/provider-stream-conformance/, the Gemini precedent crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/src/{stream.rs,translate/request.rs,live_round_trip.rs}. Read enough to give exact file paths, function names, signatures and existing test names. The spec names some line numbers; verify them.
- Probe data for fixtures: fixtures must be transcribed from real captures with FAKE signatures and FAKE redacted data. The capture files are under /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-smaschek-dev-paigasus-paigasus-helikon/ebc68a6c-86b8-4a5f-80af-4e374bf8b2aa/scratchpad/probe-840-c-claude-sonnet-4-5/ (1-turn1.sse, 16-redacted.sse) and probe-840-a/ (1-turn1.sse, empty thinking text). They hold real signatures: the plan must tell the implementer to replace every signature and redacted data value with an obvious fake (e.g. `SIG_FAKE_1`, `REDACTED_FAKE_1`) and to check with grep that no long base64 value remains. Do not copy real values into the plan.

Repo conventions to put in Global Constraints:
- Commit format `<type>(<scope>): SMA-840 <lowercase subject>`; use scope `providers` for crate code, `test` or `providers` for conformance-suite changes (check .versionrc for the allowed scopes and name the one you pick), `docs(plan)` (singular) for the plan commit, `docs(book)` or the crate scope for docs if allowed by .versionrc. End each commit message with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Commits are signed via 1Password; never bypass signing. Never `git add -A`; add explicit paths.
- No hand version bump; release-plz bumps.
- Gates per task: `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic --all-features`, plus conformance tests where touched; docs tasks also run `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --all-features --no-deps`, `npx markdownlint-cli2`, `mdbook build docs/book`.
- All docs prose (rustdoc, README, book) in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English.
- SSE fixtures stay LF (check .gitattributes covers the new fixture paths; extend if needed).
- Live tests are #[ignore] and need ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; implementers must not run them (the user runs them).
- Facade README rust fences are doctests (only relevant if touched).

Write the plan to docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-21-sma-840-anthropic-thinking-signatures.md. Right-size tasks (the SMA-827 plan had 11; aim for 7-10). Order so each task leaves the workspace green. Then commit only that file with message `docs(plan): SMA-840 add the anthropic thinking round trip plan` (with the trailer). Verify `git show --stat HEAD`.

Report back (under 300 words): the commit SHA, the task list (one line each with the files it touches), the Review Focus lines, and any spec ambiguity you had to settle (each as "Ruling: … — why").

# Subagent-Driven Development

Execute plan by dispatching a fresh implementer subagent per task, a task review (spec compliance + code quality) after each, and a broad whole-branch review at the end.

**Why subagents:** You delegate tasks to specialized agents with isolated context. By precisely crafting their instructions and context, you ensure they stay focused and succeed at their task. They should never inherit your session's context or history — you construct exactly what they need. This also preserves your own context for coordination work.

**Core principle:** Fresh subagent per task + task review (spec + quality) + broad final review = high quality, fast iteration

**Narration:** between tool calls, narrate at most one short line — the
ledger and the tool results carry the record.

**Continuous execution:** Do not pause to check in with your human partner between tasks. Execute all tasks from the plan without stopping. The only reasons to stop are the four named below, or all tasks complete. "Should I continue?" prompts and progress summaries waste their time — they asked you to execute the plan, so execute it.

**Rulings, not stalls.** A running plan does not wait on a human. Conflicts,
ambiguities, plan defects, a cap you would have asked to exceed — decide
them. The spec is the binding authority, the plan is its argument, and your
judgment settles what neither answers. Record every decision in the ledger as

going. A wrong ruling costs rework your human partner can see and undo; a
session parked on a question costs their whole day and buys nothing.

Four things stop you, and only these: an irreversible or destructive
operation; a security-sensitive action; a side effect outside this worktree
that norms say you ask about first (a merge, a push to a shared branch, a
publish); and a plan so broken that every path forward is a guess. For those,
stop and ask.

## When to Use

```dot
}
```

**vs. Executing Plans (inline):**
- Fresh subagent per task (no context pollution) instead of one context doing every task
- Review after each task (spec compliance + code quality) instead of only at the end
- Costs a fresh context per task and per review; inline costs one context plus one final reviewer
- Both run in this session, share the same plan workspace and ledger, and never pause between tasks
